title: Hollow and Garden
premise: Ivo Almeida, a mercenary whose god fell silent three years ago, survives by selling charms in a city where magic is outlawed and her old oaths are a death sentence. When the gods suddenly begin answering prayers again, Ivo discovers the silence was never abandonment but a bargain: the gods traded their voices for the country's continued existence, and now that bargain is collapsing. Hunted by the Inquisition and shadowed by a former comrade who betrayed her to survive, she must reach the Hollow Gate — the only door out of a nation being unmade — before it seals forever. In the end, Ivo chooses to stay behind and hold the gate open for others, sacrificing her own escape, and in doing so finally hears her god's voice again.
about_author: Quentin Underhill is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing defunct religious orders before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about faith, bureaucracy, and the people history forgets, and live somewhere with too much rain.

chapters.title: Small Charms
chapters.summary: Ivo sells a luck-charm to a desperate mother, hiding her magic from the city's charm-inspectors. POV: Ivo. The beat establishes her exhaustion and guilt: survival has made her small, careful, and dishonest about what she once was.

chapters.title: The First Answer
chapters.summary: A prayer Ivo mutters over a dying beggar is answered — audibly, impossibly — by her silent god. POV: Ivo. Terror and longing collide as she realizes the gods are awake again, and that someone will have noticed.

chapters.title: Inquisitor's Ledger
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Sera Vane opens a file on answered prayers across the capital and finds Ivo's name in an old heresy record. POV: Sera. The beat introduces the antagonist as principled, not cruel — a believer in law protecting people from gods.

chapters.title: The Comrade
chapters.summary: Ivo's old shield-brother Dain finds her; he betrayed her unit's location to save himself years ago and now begs her help reaching the Hollow Gate. POV: Ivo. Fury, temptation, and the bitter arithmetic of needing someone you despise.

chapters.title: What the Silence Bought
chapters.summary: In a ruined temple, a dying priest reveals the truth: the gods went silent to pay a debt keeping the country from unraveling, and the payment has run out. POV: Ivo. The beat reframes her abandonment as sacrifice, breaking something open in her.

chapters.title: Road Through Ash
chapters.summary: Ivo and Dain flee the capital as reality frays at the edges — roads looping, names vanishing from signs. Sera pursues with a warrant and doubts. POV: alternating Ivo/Sera. Rising dread and reluctant mutual respect between hunter and hunted.

chapters.title: The Price of Passage
chapters.summary: At a border shrine, the gatekeeper demands a memory as toll; Dain pays his and forgets why he ever wronged Ivo — erasing his guilt along with everything else. POV: Ivo. Horror at learning what escape truly costs.

chapters.title: Hollow Gate
chapters.summary: They reach the Gate as the country begins dissolving behind them; Sera arrives not to arrest Ivo but because her own faith has nowhere left to stand. POV: Ivo. Climactic confrontation: law, betrayal, and mercy all converge at the threshold.

chapters.title: The Doorholder
chapters.summary: The Gate can admit one more soul or stay open for the fleeing crowds — not both. Ivo chooses to hold it, anchoring herself as the anchor-stone of the door. POV: Ivo. The climax of her arc: choosing others over survival, the price paid willingly.

chapters.title: Garden
chapters.summary: On the far side, refugees rebuild; Sera carries Ivo's story like a seed. Within the Gate, Ivo tends a garden grown from the memories travelers surrendered — and hears her god speak her name at last. POV: brief coda shifting between Sera and Ivo. Quiet resolution: justice outside the law, survival redefined as what we leave open for others.
